rationale: A wins because it treats the weak spots as story material instead of wallpaper: “Without the underlying numbers this angle is a press release” is exactly the posture this announcement needs. B has usable bones, especially the study angle, but it keeps stepping past the evidence with lines like “while rivals still charge for it” and “teachers already stretched thin.” For a founder, A is closer to a real pitch map; B is a rewrite away because two angles need facts the update did not give.
gaps_in_A: “while the rest of ed-tech charges per seat” asserts competitor pricing that is not in the update. The proof caveat helps, but the headline still overclaims.
“one of the largest AI-tutoring deployments” is plausible-sounding decoration, not a supplied fact. The update gives 1 million additional students, not a market ranking.
“landing in named districts” leans on a local hook the update does not supply. The angle is valid only after Khan can name districts and put a teacher or administrator on record.
gaps_in_B: “while rivals still charge for it” is an unsupported market contrast. No competitors, pricing, or paid/free category evidence appear in the update.
“teachers already stretched thin” imports a teacher-workload/burnout peg the facts do not provide. Lesson-planning help is real; burnout relief is not yet a story.
“which tends to center on students” invents prior-coverage context. That may be true, but it is not in the supplied update.

“some teachers worry it's doing the thinking for them” overstates and narrows the fact. The update says some educators question independent thinking; it does not say teachers specifically, or that Khanmigo is “doing the thinking.”
